A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDAD study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Sections and results can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original micro-benchmark construction and reliability analyses across four benchmarks, including sensitivity, generalization, and model-size analyses in the appendices. Using cached model predictions does not negate these original analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds cluster-size diagnostics, MDAD computation timing, and results for an additional agreement threshold.

M1.justification: The agreement and MDAD procedures remain unchanged, as do the micro-benchmark selection implementations documented in v1 Appendix A and v2 Appendix B. Added explanations and threshold sensitivity results do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, MMLU-Pro, BBH, and GPQA with the same task coverage. Whole-benchmark selection, subtask selection, held-out task draws, and comparisons within model-size groups are retained.

E2.justification: The six main selection approaches remain unchanged, and the appendix retains BenTo versus uniform random sampling. Zhang et al. (2025) is newly discussed as related work, not evaluated as an additional comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 7 extends the agreement-threshold sweep from 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9 to include 0.95. The main 0.8 threshold, bucket resolution, data splits, model configurations, and micro-benchmark sizes remain unchanged; expanded partition descriptions clarify the existing protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds a cluster-size diagnostic investigating Anchor Points' stagnation at larger micro-benchmark sizes and extends threshold sensitivity analysis to 0.95. Existing generalization, bucket-resolution, trial-count, source-model-count, and model-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4 newly reports a standard deviation of 0.24 seconds for MDAD computation time. Existing bootstrap confidence intervals, trial counts, and the analysis extending to 100 trials remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: New results include the 0.95-threshold curves, mean MDAD computation time of 2.40 seconds, and cluster statistics: 47% singleton clusters for Anchor Points versus 5% for tinyBenchmarks, with the largest 10% containing half versus 21% of examples. The cluster passage switches between MMLU-Pro and MMLU, limiting direct comparison. Existing benchmark findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the mathematical definitions remain unchanged. The added statistical-power explanation and conceptual comparison table restate existing ideas rather than introduce new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims about pairwise reliability, limitations of very small subsets, and random sampling's competitiveness. The conclusion adds a future research direction without changing the demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly hypothesizes that confidence-correlation selection explains Anchor Points' strength at small sizes and that imbalanced clusters explain its stagnation at larger sizes. These mechanism explanations extend the interpretation of existing performance trends without establishing causality.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports MDAD computation cost and explicitly identifies tinyBenchmarks' clustering as k-means in the diagnostic discussion. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, per-method runtime tables, and reported code/data access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The relocated related-work section adds Zhang et al. (2025), positioning its individual-accuracy prediction findings as complementary to this paper's pairwise analysis. It also specifies independence of examples among assumptions attributed to prior power-analysis work. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 6 to Appendix A, and Discussion becomes Section 6, Discussion and Conclusion. Results gain clearer paragraph headings and case-study framing, with limited explanatory expansions and conference-header edits; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds conceptual Table 1 and a fourth threshold row to Figure 7. Main figures receive larger or simplified labels, adjusted legends and axes, and some relocation. Their basic panel structures remain intact, while existing appendix tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The additional 0.95-threshold check modestly strengthens sensitivity evidence, while Table 1, clearer figures, and computation-time reporting improve accessibility and documentation. The new cluster explanation remains tentative and inconsistently names MMLU-Pro versus MMLU, limiting its evidential value. Overall, the gains are useful but leave the central contribution and supporting results largely unchanged.
